new_statements.quote: 2.3 Tonal features / Emai is a terraced-level tone language showing high, low, and downstepped high. For some word classes, inherent tone values distinguish words that [...] have identical segments. Emai's high (H), down stepped-high (!H) and low (L) tones combine in [...] Various combinations of tone occur within lexical items. An initial high tone can be followed by a low tone, a high tone, or a down stepped high, the latter being one step lower than an immediately preceding high tone [...] Word-initial low tone can be followed by either a low tone or a high tone [...] high tone is represented by an acute accent, low tone by a grave accent, and down stepped high by an acute accent immediately followed [...]

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (uokh1238 has no catalog record and no existing statement). The work describes the Emai lect and never names Uokha (FTS 'Uokha' = 0 hits; §1 cites Elugbe 1973's dialect cluster with Ora and Iuleha); since ISO 639-3 CR 2014-043 merged Uokha [uok] into Emai-Iuleha-Ora [ema] as a place name for the same language, this language-level tonal statement (tonal, no stress statement) is the closest description and matches what the earlier snippet readers filed.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Emai (the described lect of Emai-Iuleha-Ora, into which Uokha was merged) is a terraced-level tone language with H, L and downstepped H; tone is lexically contrastive for some word classes and marked orthographically with acute/grave accents. The sketch makes no statement about word stress: full-text search of the whole scanned book returns 0 hits for stress, stressed, unstressed, 'word stress', stress* and prominence; 'accent' occurs only as the name of the tone diacritics.
new_statements.secondary_stress: none mentioned (no stress statement at all)
new_statements.exceptions: none on stress; tonal detail only (downstep one step below a preceding H; high tone spread onto low-final noun heads before certain modifiers, blocked by H-final heads)
new_statements.identity_note: The dictionary and its grammatical sketch describe the Emai lect (Afuze area, c. 20-25,000 speakers per the sketch's §1) of Emai-Iuleha-Ora; it never names Uokha. Uokha is a place name within the same language area (ISO 639-3 CR 2014-043 citing Elugbe 1989: 22-24; Egbokhare 2011: 68 puts Uokha in Oyakhire's 1997 dialect group A with Emai, Ora, Iuleha), so the statement applies to uokh1238 only at language level, as the closest available description; no Uokha-specific phonological description is known.
